counterexamples.description: Known petrification lowers surprise effect and speed, not immunity.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Prior knowledge weakens surprise recognition washing, slower body stiffening.
counterexamples.explanation: Known petrification lowers surprise effect and speed, not immunity.

contexts.japanese: ……ですが昨日ほどの効果は望めないでしょう。貴方は私の魔眼が石化だと知っている。不意打ちによる認識洗浄は弱まっていますから、体が硬直するスピードは落ちる筈です」
contexts.english: ...However, you can expect them to have a lesser effect than they did yesterday. As you know, my Mystic Eyes have the power of Petrification. The cognitive erasure they cause when the target is taken by surprise is weakened, so your body should not petrify as quickly."

counterexamples.description: Off-guard condition increases effect again.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Situation dependent, lack vigilance boosts power.
counterexamples.explanation: Off-guard condition increases effect again.

contexts.japanese: 「状況によります。貴方が気を抜いていれば、魔眼の効果は上がるでしょう」
contexts.english: "That depends on the situation. If you let your guard down, the Mystic Eyes would have an increased effect."

counterexamples.description: No-danger assurance explicitly limited to not killing.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Won't take life; in that sense no danger.
counterexamples.explanation: No-danger assurance explicitly limited to not killing.

contexts.japanese: 「そうですね。私は貴方の命は取りません。そういった意味で言えば、なんの危険もありませんが」
contexts.english: "That is true. I will not kill you. In that sense, there is no danger to your life."

counterexamples.description: Other eye effects unspecified.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Eyes more than petrification.
counterexamples.explanation: Other eye effects unspecified.

contexts.japanese: 「だめ、だめったらだめですっ……！　ライダーの眼は石化だけじゃないんだからっ！」
contexts.english: "No! No means no! Rider's eyes do more than just petrify people!"

counterexamples.description: Deploying Rider shortens remaining life.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Obey command but action cuts her remaining time, asks assent.
counterexamples.explanation: Deploying Rider shortens remaining life.

contexts.japanese: 「……命令ならば従います。ですがサクラ。貴女の体とて長くはない。私を行使するという事は、貴女の余命を削る事です。それでもいいのですね？」
contexts.english: "...I'll go if you if you order it. But Sakura, your body will not last much longer. Having me act will only shorten your remaining life. Are you sure about this?"

counterexamples.description: Noble Phantasm use is future necessity requiring assent.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Ill wind, will use treasure, okay?
counterexamples.explanation: Noble Phantasm use is future necessity requiring assent.

contexts.japanese: 「……よくない風です。宝具を使用する事になりますが、構いませんね」
contexts.english: "...This is an ill breeze. I will need to use my Noble Phantasm, if you don't mind."

counterexamples.description: Order prioritizes carrying Sakura away over costly battle.
counterexamples.sourceReading: If elder appears avoid consuming magic, carry and run; Rider speed protects.
counterexamples.explanation: Order prioritizes carrying Sakura away over costly battle.

contexts.japanese: もし臓硯が来たら魔力を消費する戦闘は避けて、桜を抱きかかえて逃げること。ライダーの足なら追いつかれる事はないだろ」
contexts.english: If Zouken shows up, avoid fighting since that will use magical energy. Take Sakura and run. He won't be able to keep up with you."

counterexamples.description: Route memory and intuition from magic remain.
counterexamples.sourceReading: No map/compass, guidance from Illya magic, relies memory and instinct.
counterexamples.explanation: Route memory and intuition from magic remain.

contexts.japanese: もともとイリヤの魔術によって得た直感である。なら、頼りになるのは見せられた記憶と、自身の直感だけだろう。
contexts.english: I still have the sense of direction I got from the magecraft Illya cast on me. All I can do is rely on the memory of what I saw, and my own intuition.

contexts.japanese: 地図、コンパスといった物は持ってこなかった。
contexts.english: I don't have a map or a compass.

counterexamples.description: Outside energy supply needed to stabilize morning power.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Stable energy indicates replenishment; otherwise fever recurring.
counterexamples.explanation: Outside energy supply needed to stabilize morning power.

contexts.japanese: 「……そのようですね。朝、サクラの魔力は安定していました。外部からの供給がなければ、サクラはまた熱に魘されていたでしょう。
contexts.english: "...It appears so. Her magical energy was stable this morning. Without an external supply of energy, she would have suffered from another fever.

counterexamples.description: He embraces Grail use for happiness rather than simply disclaiming gain.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Actually would use as much if makes Sakura happy.
counterexamples.explanation: He embraces Grail use for happiness rather than simply disclaiming gain.

contexts.japanese: 「いや、するよ。聖杯がなんであるかは知らないけど、それが桜を幸せにしてくれるんだったらいくらでも使ってやる」
contexts.english: "Oh, I'll use it. I don't know what the Holy Grail is, but I'll use it as much as it takes to make her happy."

contexts.japanese: 「……では、貴方はサクラの為に戦うのですね？　目的はあくまでサクラの体を救う為。サクラに聖杯を獲らせ、自分の益とする気はないと？」
contexts.english: "...And will you fight for her sake? You say that your goal is to heal her body. Will you give her the Holy Grail and not use it for your own benefit?"

counterexamples.description: Sparse wildlife is attributed tentatively to Einzbern magic.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Probably their magecraft causes absence of living presence.
counterexamples.explanation: Sparse wildlife is attributed tentatively to Einzbern magic.

contexts.japanese: 生き物の気配が希薄なのは、アインツベルンの魔術によるものなのだろう。
contexts.english: The lack of local wildlife is probably due to Einzbern magecraft.

counterexamples.description: Strengthening takes several minutes.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Stops, concentrates, reinforces wooden sword over minutes.
counterexamples.explanation: Strengthening takes several minutes.

contexts.japanese: ……足を止めて意識を集中させ、数分かけて木刀に“強化”をかける。
contexts.english: I stop, concentrate, and take a few minutes to Strengthen my sword.

counterexamples.description: Illya recognizes Zouken from homeland instruction, not prior meeting.
counterexamples.sourceReading: At glance matches Makiri-associated magus taught before departure.
counterexamples.explanation: Illya recognizes Zouken from homeland instruction, not prior meeting.

contexts.japanese: それが故郷の城を出る時に教えられた、同朋の魔術師である事は一目で判った。
contexts.english: She recognizes him with a single look as a mage of the Makiris, whom she was taught about when she left the castle in her homeland.

counterexamples.description: Public ritual premise is explicitly distorted.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Masters-chosen/Servants-formed story deliberately transmitted crookedly.
counterexamples.explanation: Public ritual premise is explicitly distorted.

contexts.japanese: その前提は、意図的に歪められて伝わったものだ。
contexts.english: That rule—that pretext was deliberately distorted and spread.

counterexamples.description: Masters and Servants retain ritual-component roles.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Masters prepared as one part; Servants open gate.
counterexamples.explanation: Masters and Servants retain ritual-component roles.

contexts.japanese: マスターは選ばれるのではなく、ただ儀式の一端として用意されるだけのもの。
contexts.english: The Masters are not chosen. They are merely components of a ritual.

contexts.japanese: そしてサーヴァントとは、ただ門を開ける為だけのもの—
contexts.english: Likewise, Servants are merely used to open the gate...

counterexamples.description: Vessel and Greater Grail wills remain distinct.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Vessel no will; Greater Grail selects Masters.
counterexamples.explanation: Vessel and Greater Grail wills remain distinct.

contexts.japanese: 器になる聖杯に意思はないけど、マスターを選び出す大聖杯には意思があるわ。もともとこの土地に原型があるからこそ、貴方たちは英霊を呼び出して聖杯を満たそうとした。
contexts.english: The vessel has no will of it own, but the Greater Grail which selects the Masters does. You summon Heroic Spirits to fill the Holy Grail because its prototype is here, on this land.

counterexamples.description: Original miracle aspiration remains an unanswered question.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Asks where shared earnest wish came from and its purpose.
counterexamples.explanation: Original miracle aspiration remains an unanswered question.

contexts.japanese: 「思い出しなさい。わたしたちの悲願、奇跡に至ろうとする切望は何処からきたものなのか。
contexts.english: "Remember. Where did our wish, our earnest hope to achieve a miracle, come from?

counterexamples.description: The unidentified heat is explicitly felt resonating with the Noble Phantasm.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He knows neither identity nor reason.
counterexamples.explanation: The unidentified heat is explicitly felt resonating with the Noble Phantasm.

contexts.japanese: 正体は掴めず理由も定かではないが、この熱は今の宝具と共鳴したものだと感じ取れた。
contexts.english: I don't know what or why, but I sense this heat resonating with the Noble Phantasm that was just unleashed.

counterexamples.description: Shirou models the arm as dumping excess heat into his body.
counterexamples.sourceReading: This is his explanation, not neutral verified mechanics.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou models the arm as dumping excess heat into his body.

contexts.japanese: それが左腕の中で溜まりきって一杯になった時、処理しきれない熱を体側に逃がす。
contexts.english: Once enough heat builds up in the arm, it gets dumped into my body.

counterexamples.description: Archer's Noble Phantasm is not simply the paired blades.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The denial precedes the forging/Projection account.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer's Noble Phantasm is not simply the paired blades.

contexts.japanese: 一対の短剣が、ではない。
contexts.english: Not those short swords.

counterexamples.description: Seen and understood objects can be reproduced.
counterexamples.sourceReading: This is experienced knowledge within the dream.
counterexamples.explanation: Seen and understood objects can be reproduced.

contexts.japanese: 目に見たもの、理解したものならばいくらでも複製する。
contexts.english: He could reproduce anything he saw and understood.

counterexamples.description: The ability is Projection rather than ordinary copying.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The terminology distinction is explicit.
counterexamples.explanation: The ability is Projection rather than ordinary copying.

contexts.japanese: それは複製ではなく投影。
contexts.english: It wasn't reproduction, but Projection—

counterexamples.description: The invasive heat demands mastery.
counterexamples.sourceReading: This is internal coercive sensation, not calm instruction.
counterexamples.explanation: The invasive heat demands mastery.

contexts.japanese: それを—使いこなせと、心を燃やす熱が言った。
contexts.english: The heat burning my heart demands that I master it.

counterexamples.description: The arm was detached and connected while Archer remained in the world.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou's circuits and energy sustain it as flesh.
counterexamples.explanation: The arm was detached and connected while Archer remained in the world.

contexts.japanese: 「移植が終わる前に消滅したのなら、その左腕も消えていただろう。だがおまえのソレはアーチャーが現世に留まっているうちに切り離し、おまえの体に植え付けたものだ。衛宮士郎の魔術回路と繋げ、おまえ自身の魔力で現世に受肉させている英霊の肉。
contexts.english: "If he had passed on before the transplant was complete, then the arm would have gone as well. But your new arm was amputated and transplanted while he was still in the mortal world. It is the incarnated flesh of a Heroic Spirit, connected to Shirou Emiya's Magic Circuits and incarnated by your own magical energy.

counterexamples.description: Illya distinguishes spiritual healing from ordinary bodily medicine.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She recognizes Kirei's genuine skill.
counterexamples.explanation: Illya distinguishes spiritual healing from ordinary bodily medicine.

contexts.japanese: 「繋げるだけなら出来なくもないわ。霊媒の医師は肉体ではなく魂を癒すものだっていうし、そこの神父は見かけによらず本物だったっていう事ね」
contexts.english: "It isn't impossible to connect them. It's said that spiritual healers treat the soul, not the body, and that priest turned out to be a real one, despite all appearances."

counterexamples.description: Kirei says soul restoration is beyond magecraft.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He expected physical success followed by shock death.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei says soul restoration is beyond magecraft.

contexts.japanese: 霊体……魂の蘇生、復元は魔術では扱えない神秘である。故に今回も、形だけ成功した後でショック死すると思ったのだが—」
contexts.english: The resurrection and restoration of spiritual bodies...of souls is a Mystic beyond the scope of magecraft. That is why I expected it to work only in shape, and that you would die of shock afterward..."

counterexamples.description: Compatibility applies to circuits only.
counterexamples.sourceReading: It does not make Heroic Spirit power safe for a human.
counterexamples.explanation: Compatibility applies to circuits only.

contexts.japanese: 「だが注意しろ。私が言っているのは、あくまで回路が合う、というだけの話だ。
contexts.english: "But be warned. I am only saying that your circuits were compatible.

counterexamples.description: The wrapping separates left-arm circuits from Shirou's spellcasting.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Magecraft elsewhere does not activate it as part of him.
counterexamples.explanation: The wrapping separates left-arm circuits from Shirou's spellcasting.

contexts.japanese: 「ああ、その為の封印だ。それを巻いているかぎり、左腕は魔術回路を発現しない。おまえが魔術を使おうと、その左腕だけは別の物として扱われる。
contexts.english: "Yes, they are a seal. So long as your left arm stays wrapped, its Magic Circuits will not manifest. Even if you use magecraft, the left arm won't act as a part of you.

counterexamples.description: Rin hopes not to find the suspected inheritance.
counterexamples.sourceReading: If it is what she imagines, she cannot handle it alone.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin hopes not to find the suspected inheritance.

contexts.japanese: ……けど、出来れば見つけたくない。遠坂の遺産、大師父の置き土産が想像通りのものなら、わたしだけじゃどうにもならないから」
contexts.english: ...Though, I'd like to avoid digging up any Tohsaka heirlooms if we can help it. If Grandmaster Kischur's souvenirs are what I think they are, I can't handle them by myself."

counterexamples.description: Shirou repeats unfamiliar name fragments in confusion.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He does not recognize the figure or object.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou repeats unfamiliar name fragments in confusion.

contexts.japanese: 「………きしゅあ？　ぜる？　しゅばいんおーぐ？」
contexts.english: "...Kissher? Zel? Shavineorg?"

counterexamples.description: Illya's apparent age is judged unreliable for an exceptional magus.
counterexamples.sourceReading: No concrete real age is supplied.
counterexamples.explanation: Illya's apparent age is judged unreliable for an exceptional magus.

contexts.japanese: あれだけのサーヴァントを従えるマスターなら、さぞ卓越した魔術師だろう。となると、見かけの肉体年齢はあまり当てに出来るものじゃない。
contexts.english: She'd need to be a next-level mage to command such a strong Servant. That means her apparent physical age might be misleading.

counterexamples.description: Shirou sees the Emiya household as outside the Association.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He invokes Kiritsugu as precedent for ignoring rules.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou sees the Emiya household as outside the Association.

contexts.japanese: 協会が決めた規則に従ったところで何か貰える訳でもなし、切嗣同様無視してもかまわない。
contexts.english: I won't get anything out of following the Association's laws, so I can just ignore them like my old man did.

counterexamples.description: Kiritsugu is retained as a hired Master.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He was employed as a Master rather than born into the participating family.
counterexamples.explanation: Kiritsugu is retained as a hired Master.

contexts.japanese: 「結論として、衛宮切嗣はマスターとして雇われた。
contexts.english: "Regardless, Kiritsugu Emiya was hired as a Master.

counterexamples.description: Einzbern combat weakness motivates recruiting Kiritsugu.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The family is ill suited to combat and entrusts hope to an unaffiliated killer skilled in killing contests.
counterexamples.explanation: Einzbern combat weakness motivates recruiting Kiritsugu.

contexts.japanese: 実際、アインツベルンの魔術は戦闘向きではない。彼らは戦いには不向きな一族だ。それ故に、殺し合いに長け、魔術協会に属さなかった切嗣に望みを託した」
contexts.english: In fact, the Einzbern mages themselves are not suited to fighting. Their clan is particularly ill-suited to it. Thus, they placed their hopes on Kiritsugu, a seasoned killer without ties to the Mage's Association."

counterexamples.description: Marriage, Master power and a combat-oriented heir remain distinct benefits.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Einzbern gives the heretic Grail knowledge and Master power and joins him to its bloodline to produce a more battle-ready successor.
counterexamples.explanation: Marriage, Master power and a combat-oriented heir remain distinct benefits.

contexts.japanese: 「異端である切嗣に聖杯の知識を与え、マスターとしての力を与え、アインツベルンの血と交わる事で、より戦闘向きの後継者を産み出しもした。
contexts.english: "They taught him—a heretic—knowledge of the Holy Grail, gave him the powers of a Master, and had him join with their bloodline in order to produce an even more battle-worthy heir.

counterexamples.description: Einzbern withdrawal and ten-year preparation remain chronological.
counterexamples.sourceReading: After Kiritsugu's betrayal the family retreats and spends ten years preparing the next Grail.
counterexamples.explanation: Einzbern withdrawal and ten-year preparation remain chronological.

contexts.japanese: 切嗣に裏切られたアインツベルンは撤退し、次の聖杯の用意に十年を費やした」
contexts.english: After Kiritsugu's treachery, the Einzberns retreated and have spent the last decade preparing for the next Holy Grail."

counterexamples.description: Kiritsugu's dream remains impossible even through the impossible Grail.
counterexamples.sourceReading: His dream is magic that cannot come true except through the impossible thing called the Grail, and still ought not be realizable.
counterexamples.explanation: Kiritsugu's dream remains impossible even through the impossible Grail.

contexts.japanese: 衛宮切嗣という男の夢は、聖杯という“あり得ないもの”でしか叶わない、叶う筈のない魔法だった」
contexts.english: The dream of Kiritsugu Emiya was an impossible, magical idea that only an impossible device like the Holy Grail could make come true."

counterexamples.description: The three-family ritual remains rooted in a leyline distortion two centuries earlier.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Mages share secret arts and build an activation formation deep in the land.
counterexamples.explanation: The three-family ritual remains rooted in a leyline distortion two centuries earlier.

contexts.japanese: 「二百年前、この地の霊脈に歪みがあると知った魔術師たちがいてな。彼らは互いに秘術を提供しあい、聖杯を起動させる陣をこの地の深くに作り上げた。
contexts.english: "Two hundred years ago, there was a group of mages who learned of a distortion in this land's leylines. They shared their secrets with each other and built a circle deep within the land to activate the Holy Grail.

counterexamples.description: The three founding contributions remain differentiated.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Creation of Grail, Command Spells, and land plus world-opening art are separate.
counterexamples.explanation: The three founding contributions remain differentiated.

contexts.japanese: 「聖杯を作り上げたもの。英霊を酷使する令呪を考案したもの。土地を提供し、世界に孔をうがつ秘術を提供したもの」
contexts.english: "Those who created the Holy Grail. Those who conceived the Command Spells with which to bind Heroic Spirits to their will. Those who provided the land and the ritual to open a path leading beyond the world."

counterexamples.description: Einzbern's current vessel-making role remains explicit.
counterexamples.sourceReading: After failed summoning and uncertain ownership, its present role is making the Grail vessel.
counterexamples.explanation: Einzbern's current vessel-making role remains explicit.

contexts.japanese: 今では聖杯の器を作り上げるだけの役割だ。
contexts.english: Their current role is only to create a vessel for the Holy Grail.

counterexamples.description: Kirei offers conditional treatment for victims.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The Church cannot overlook casualties; if they arrive in time, Kirei will treat them.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei offers conditional treatment for victims.

contexts.japanese: 犠牲者を出すのは教会としても見過ごせないのでな。間に合うのなら、こちらで治療は引き受けよう」
contexts.english: The Church mustn't overlook any victims. I will treat them, if you can bring them here in time."

counterexamples.description: A prior death motivates Kirei to learn healing.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Someone with fatal illness died before him, prompting a field for which he proved suited.
counterexamples.explanation: A prior death motivates Kirei to learn healing.

contexts.japanese: 昔、目の前で死病つきに死なれてな。それを機に手を染めてみたのだが、思いの外相性が良かったようだ」
contexts.english: Long ago, I watched someone die of illness. It spurred me to try my hand at healing, and I had a greater knack for it than I expected."

counterexamples.description: Leyline disturbance supports Saber's active hunt.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Disruption convinces her other Masters are moving; choice may let them reduce the field by one tonight.
counterexamples.explanation: Leyline disturbance supports Saber's active hunt.

contexts.japanese: —どちらの町にも言える事ですが、地脈の流れに僅かな支障が起きています。他のマスターが行動を起こしているのは間違いないでしょう。選択次第では、今夜中に一人減らせる」
contexts.english: We could go to either side of the city, but there is a slight disruption in the flow of the leylines. There's no doubt that the other Masters are active. Depending on our choices tonight, we may be able to defeat one of them."

counterexamples.description: The sensed event remains both a scream and magical aftereffect.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou identifies a scream and wake of strong mana.
counterexamples.explanation: The sensed event remains both a scream and magical aftereffect.

contexts.japanese: だが、今のは間違いなく誰かの悲鳴であり、強い魔力の余波だった。
contexts.english: But it was unmistakably a scream accompanied by a strong wave of magical energy.

counterexamples.description: The mental lock remains a simile tied to circuit activation.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou locks his heart as he would put a circuit pseudo-nerve into his back.
counterexamples.explanation: The mental lock remains a simile tied to circuit activation.

contexts.japanese: 背中に魔術回路を入れるように、心に鍵をかけて新都へ歩き出した。
contexts.english: I steel myself as we walk, just like I do when I insert the pseudo-nerve of a Magic Circuit into my back.

counterexamples.description: The alternate branch locates a Servant in the park below.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Saber senses a Servant immediately below the bridge.
counterexamples.explanation: The alternate branch locates a Servant in the park below.

contexts.japanese: 「サーヴァントの気配です。場所はすぐ下の公園のようですが」
contexts.english: "I sense a Servant. It appears to be in the park right below us."

counterexamples.description: The contaminated-mana simile remains a clear stream fouled by oil.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou compares the ominous dense energy to heavy oil in clear water.
counterexamples.explanation: The contaminated-mana simile remains a clear stream fouled by oil.

contexts.japanese: 清流の中に重油が流れているようなもの。
contexts.english: It's like an oil spill in the middle of a clear stream.

counterexamples.description: Rider drains mind and memory rather than flesh.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou perceives the victim's inner human contents being sucked up.
counterexamples.explanation: Rider drains mind and memory rather than flesh.

contexts.japanese: あの黒い装束の女は、人間の中身—精神とか記憶とか、そういったモノを吸い上げている。
contexts.english: The woman in black was sucking on a person's entire being: her victim's mind and memories.

counterexamples.description: Rider disappears with the destroyed book.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Her form vanishes without trace at the same time.
counterexamples.explanation: Rider disappears with the destroyed book.

contexts.japanese: ライダーの姿も、跡形もなく消え去った。
contexts.english: Rider disappears without a trace.

counterexamples.description: Zouken's denial remains attributed and temporally framed.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He claims he once considered the sister, but now would not send an ignorant grandchild into the war.
counterexamples.explanation: Zouken's denial remains attributed and temporally framed.

contexts.japanese: ……まあ、兄が使い物にならなければ妹を、とも思っておったが、既に勝敗は決した。今更、何も知らぬ孫を聖杯戦争に駆り出す事もなかろうよ」
contexts.english: ...I did consider the sister if the brother turned out to be of no use, but our role in this contest has already concluded. There's little point in sending out an ignorant grandchild to fight in the Holy Grail War."

counterexamples.description: Mana residue remains an indirect clue.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Patrolling for traces may yield clues to other Masters.
counterexamples.explanation: Mana residue remains an indirect clue.

contexts.japanese: それを頼りに街を巡回していれば、他のマスターの手がかりぐらいは得られるだろう。
contexts.english: If I canvass the city looking for those traces, then I might find clues leading to the other Masters.

counterexamples.description: The energy scale retains its key values.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Recovery eight, maintenance six, reserve two, Lancer fifty and Berserker two hundred.
counterexamples.explanation: The energy scale retains its key values.

contexts.japanese: セイバーの一日の魔力回復量が８だとすると、肉体維持に必要な魔力は６。んで、余剰の２が貯められる貯金になる。
contexts.english: You recover eight points of magical energy a day, and it takes six to maintain your body. That leaves two in reserve.

contexts.japanese: シロウ風に言うのなら、ランサーとの戦いに五十、バーサーカーとの戦いにいたっては二百ほど魔力を消費しました」
contexts.english: To use your terms, I spent fifty points in my skirmish with Lancer, and two hundred fighting Berserker."

counterexamples.description: The ten-point fight explicitly requires no wounds or armor damage.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Saber limits the low estimate to untouched body and armor.
counterexamples.explanation: The ten-point fight explicitly requires no wounds or armor damage.

contexts.japanese: 「こちらが一度も傷を負わず、鎧を破損しない限りはそうです。ですが同格の英霊相手ではそのような事はあり得ません。
contexts.english: "Only as long as I avoid being wounded and my armor stays intact. But that is very unlikely if I fight a Heroic Spirit of similar strength.

counterexamples.description: Armor repair costs more than flesh healing.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Most of Saber's energy is fixed in defense.
counterexamples.explanation: Armor repair costs more than flesh healing.

contexts.japanese: 「肉体の治癒にはそう魔力を使いません。むしろ破壊された鎧の修復の方が大きい。私の魔力は、その大半を守りに固定していますから」
contexts.english: "It doesn't take much energy to heal my physical body. In fact, it costs more to restore my damaged armor. Most of my magical energy is dedicated to my defenses."

counterexamples.description: Saber cannot take spirit form and saves energy by dismissing armor.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Other Servants likely reduce Master burden in spirit form.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber cannot take spirit form and saves energy by dismissing armor.

contexts.japanese: 「はい。ですが、他のサーヴァントにその必要はないでしょう。私は霊体になれないので武装を解除するしかありませんが、ランサーやアーチャーは非戦闘時に霊体になる事でマスターへの負担を減らしている筈です」
contexts.english: "Yes. But other Servants have no such requirements. Unlike Lancer or Archer who can assume spirit form outside of combat to reduce the burden on their Masters, I can only dispel my armor."

counterexamples.description: Current reserve is about one thousand, not a maximum.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Saber gives an approximate present quantity in Shirou's scale.
counterexamples.explanation: Current reserve is about one thousand, not a maximum.

contexts.japanese: 「シロウ風に言うのなら、一千ほどですが」
contexts.english: "In your terms, about a thousand points."

counterexamples.description: Noble Phantasm cost remains a separate limitation.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Current Saber would have difficulty using it despite ordinary combat reserve.
counterexamples.explanation: Noble Phantasm cost remains a separate limitation.

contexts.japanese: 先ほども言いましたが、宝具の使用には莫大な魔力を必要とします。今の私では宝具の使用は厳しい。その為に、少しでも魔力を温存しなくてはならないのです」
contexts.english: As I said, my Noble Phantasm requires an enormous amount of magical energy. It would be quite difficult to use it in this state. That is why I should try to conserve energy whenever possible."

counterexamples.description: The mana problem remains unsolved.
counterexamples.sourceReading: They can only understand the current situation, not fix supply.
counterexamples.explanation: The mana problem remains unsolved.

contexts.japanese: もとより俺たちではどうしようもない問題だし、解決策は現状を把握するぐらいしかない。
contexts.english: It isn't something we have a solution for, so the next step is to get a firm grasp on our situation.

counterexamples.description: The Master obtains the Grail through the Servant before the Servant's wish.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Saber explains the order as part of their relationship.
counterexamples.explanation: The Master obtains the Grail through the Servant before the Servant's wish.

contexts.japanese: 聖杯戦争に勝利したマスターは、サーヴァントを介して聖杯を手に入れる。その後、サーヴァントは見返りとして望みを叶える。
contexts.english: The Master who is victorious in the Holy Grail War will obtain the Holy Grail through their Servant. Afterwards, the Servant's wish will be granted in repayment.

counterexamples.description: Class names are explicitly role labels rather than true names.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Saber offers a rough explanation.
counterexamples.explanation: Class names are explicitly role labels rather than true names.

contexts.japanese: 「ええ、私たちの呼び名は役割毎につけられた呼称にすぎません。……そうですね、この際ですから大まかに説明してしまいましょう」
contexts.english: "Yes, those are only names that are given based on each of our roles... All right, I shall use this as an opportunity to give a rough explanation."

counterexamples.description: Recorded heroic weakness motivates true-name secrecy.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Identity reveals exploitable weaknesses.
counterexamples.explanation: Recorded heroic weakness motivates true-name secrecy.

contexts.japanese: 「ですが、それは同時に短所でもあります。私たちは英霊であるが故に、その弱点を記録に残している。
contexts.english: "But at the same time, that is also our weakness. Because Heroic Spirits each left a mark upon history, our weaknesses were also recorded.

contexts.japanese: 名を明かす—正体を明かすという事は、その弱点をさらけ出す事になります。
contexts.english: By revealing our names and identities, we would be revealing our weaknesses.

counterexamples.description: Seven preformed vessels solve seven full summonings.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Compatible spirits are called into supports for existence in this world.
counterexamples.explanation: Seven preformed vessels solve seven full summonings.

contexts.japanese: 「そうです。もとより英霊をまるごと召喚する、という事自体が奇蹟に近い。それを七人分、というのは聖杯でも手に余る。
contexts.english: "That is correct. First of all, summoning a Heroic Spirit is itself close to a miracle. To summon seven of them is too much even for the Holy Grail.

contexts.japanese: その解決の為、聖杯は予め七つの器を用意し、その器に適合する英霊だけを呼び寄せた。この世界に我々が存在できる依り代を用意したのです。
contexts.english: In order to solve that, the Holy Grail prepares seven vessels beforehand and only calls forth Heroic Spirits who are compatible with those vessels. Such vessels are like objects that keep us temporarily bound to this world.

counterexamples.description: All seven classes remain present and ordered.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The list runs Saber through Berserker.
counterexamples.explanation: All seven classes remain present and ordered.

contexts.japanese: セイバー、
contexts.english: Saber,

contexts.japanese: バーサーカー。
contexts.english: and Berserker.

counterexamples.description: Saber class follows sword excellence.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou infers her suitability for the sword class.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber class follows sword excellence.

contexts.japanese: 「……なるほど。じゃあセイバーは剣に優れた英霊だから、セイバーとして呼ばれたって事か」
contexts.english: "...I get it. So you're a Saber because you're a Heroic Spirit who was good with a sword."

counterexamples.description: Assassin concealment and Caster's anachronistic magecraft remain distinct threats.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Simple power comparison is insufficient.
counterexamples.explanation: Assassin concealment and Caster's anachronistic magecraft remain distinct threats.

contexts.japanese: 「アサシンのサーヴァントは能力こそ低いですが気配を隠すという能力がありますし、キャスターのサーヴァントはこの時代にない魔術に精通している。
contexts.english: "The Assassin Servant lacks combat capacity but has the ability to hide its presence, and the Caster Servant is proficient in magecraft that does not exist in this age.

counterexamples.description: Lancer's spear is already a Noble Phantasm before activation.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Mana and True Name reveal its full value.
counterexamples.explanation: Lancer's spear is already a Noble Phantasm before activation.

contexts.japanese: たとえばランサーの槍です。彼の槍はそれ自体が宝具ではありますが、その真価を発揮するのは魔力を注ぎ込み、その真名を口にした時だけです」
contexts.english: As you say, Lancer's spear. It is a Noble Phantasm, but its true value is demonstrated only when he puts magical energy into it and says its True Name."

counterexamples.description: True-name recitation activates and reveals identity.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Activation is compared with an incantation.
counterexamples.explanation: True-name recitation activates and reveals identity.

contexts.japanese: 魔術の発現に詠唱が必要なように、宝具の発動にも詠唱—真名による覚醒が必要になる。
contexts.english: Just as incantations are necessary to activate magecraft, Noble Phantasms also need their True Name to be recited in order to awaken and activate them.

contexts.japanese: ですが、これにも危険はあります。宝具の真名を口にすれば、そのサーヴァントの正体が判ってしまう」
contexts.english: However, this also has its dangers. By saying the True Name of the Noble Phantasm, that Servant's identity will be revealed."

counterexamples.description: A Noble Phantasm trades identity exposure for a decisive blow.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Failure exposes weakness.
counterexamples.explanation: A Noble Phantasm trades identity exposure for a decisive blow.

contexts.japanese: 正体を明かすかわりに、避けきれぬ必殺の一撃を炸裂させる。
contexts.english: In exchange for revealing the identity, it would launch an unavoidable fatal blow.

contexts.japanese: だがそれが不発に終わった時—そのサーヴァントは、自らの欠点をもさらけ出す事になる。
contexts.english: And if that attack misses or fails, the Servant has revealed their weaknesses.

counterexamples.description: Saber gives only an equivocal confirmation about the invisible sword.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She says its identity remains unrevealed.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber gives only an equivocal confirmation about the invisible sword.

contexts.japanese: 「……そうですね。ですが、あれはまだ正体を明かしていません。今の状態で私の真名を知るサーヴァントはいないでしょう」
contexts.english: "...Yes. However, I have not revealed its identity yet. At this point, there should not be any Servants who know my True Name."

counterexamples.description: Mind-reading remains a hypothetical risk.
counterexamples.sourceReading: A superior mage might read inexperienced Shirou's thoughts.
counterexamples.explanation: Mind-reading remains a hypothetical risk.

contexts.japanese: 優れた魔術師ならば、シロウの思考を読む事も可能でしょう。ですから—」
contexts.english: If you encounter a superior mage, they should be able to read your mind. Therefore..."

counterexamples.description: Servant sensing requires proximity and is easier in physical form.
counterexamples.sourceReading: A Servant itself is detectable mana.
counterexamples.explanation: Servant sensing requires proximity and is easier in physical form.

contexts.japanese: ただ、近くにいるのならサーヴァントはサーヴァントの気配を察知できます。それが実体化しているのなら尚更です。サーヴァントはそれ自体が強力な魔力ですから。
contexts.english: But if other Servants are near, a Servant can sense their presence. All the more so if they are in physical form. Servants themselves are a powerful force of magical energy.

counterexamples.description: Two years near Rin demonstrate Shirou's poor mage detection.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He repeatedly saw her without recognizing her identity.
counterexamples.explanation: Two years near Rin demonstrate Shirou's poor mage detection.

contexts.japanese: そもそも同じ学校にいた遠坂の正体にも気づかなかったんだぞ、俺は。
contexts.english: I mean, I didn't even realize Tohsaka's identity, and we go to the same school.

contexts.japanese: 二年間も同じ建物にいて、あまつさえ何度も見かけているっていうのにだ。
contexts.english: We were in the same building for two years, and on top of that, I saw her many times.

counterexamples.description: The forehead point is Saber's fingertip, not a blade.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She instructs him to focus on it and sense mana.
counterexamples.explanation: The forehead point is Saber's fingertip, not a blade.

contexts.japanese: 「……。マスター、黙って私の指先に意識を集中してください。貴方も魔術師なら、それでこちらの魔力を感じ取れるでしょう」
contexts.english: "...Master, please be quiet and concentrate on my fingertip. If you are a mage, you should be able to feel my magical energy from that."

contexts.japanese: そうか、触れてるのはセイバーの指か。
contexts.english: Oh, so it's Saber's finger touching me.

counterexamples.description: Master perception varies by individual representation.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Colors and beasts are examples, not universal displays.
counterexamples.explanation: Master perception varies by individual representation.

contexts.japanese: 「どのようなカタチで把握したのかは知りません。サーヴァントの能力を測るのは、あくまでシロウが見る基準です。単純に色で識別するマスターもいれば、獣に喩えて見分けるマスターもいます」
contexts.english: "I do not know how you saw it. Your standards are what sets how you measure a Servant's ability. There are some Masters who distinguish simply through colors, and there are other Masters who understand by comparing them to beasts."

counterexamples.description: Once-seen targets can be checked in more detail.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Saber calls this a basic Master function and asks frequent checking.
counterexamples.explanation: Once-seen targets can be checked in more detail.

contexts.japanese: これはマスターとしての基本ですから、今後は頻繁に確かめてください。私と同様、一度見た相手ならばその詳細が理解出来ている筈ですから」
contexts.english: This is a fundamental part of being a Master, so from now on, please check frequently. You should be able to understand the details of someone after seeing them once."

counterexamples.description: Rin keeps the Servant-link mechanism qualified.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She proposes a powerful Saber, a summoning mistake or both, connected by some line.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin keeps the Servant-link mechanism qualified.

contexts.japanese: 「そうなると原因はサーヴァントね。
contexts.english: "Which means it must be your Servant.

contexts.japanese: 貴方のサーヴァントはよっぽど強力なのか、それとも召喚の時に何か手違いが生じたのか。……ま、両方だと思うけど、何らかのラインが繋がったんでしょうね」
contexts.english: Either your Servant is pretty powerful, or something happened when you summoned them... I think it's both, actually, but you must be connected by some line."

counterexamples.description: The abnormal reverse flow of a familiar's ability remains explicit.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Saber's regeneration may flow to Shirou, reversing the usual mage-to-familiar grant.
counterexamples.explanation: The abnormal reverse flow of a familiar's ability remains explicit.

contexts.japanese: 「見たところセイバーには自然治癒の力もあるみたいだから、それが貴方に流れてるんじゃないかな。
contexts.english: "Saber can evidently regenerate too, so her power might be flowing into you.

contexts.japanese: 普通は魔術師の能力が使い魔に付与されるんだけど、貴方の場合は使い魔の特殊能力が主人を助けてるってワケ」
contexts.english: Normally the mage's abilities are shared with their familiar, but in your case, the familiar's abilities are helping the Master."

counterexamples.description: The upstream-river analogy and Saber's exceptional power remain intact.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou supplies the image and Rin accepts it as normally impossible.
counterexamples.explanation: The upstream-river analogy and Saber's exceptional power remain intact.

contexts.japanese: 「……む。簡単に言って、川の水が下から上に流れているようなもんか？」
contexts.english: "Hm. So it's like a river flowing upstream?"

contexts.japanese: 「上手い喩えね。本来ならあり得ないだろうけど、セイバーの魔力ってのは川の流れを変えるほど膨大なんでしょう。そうでなければあの体格でバーサーカーとまともに打ち合うなんて考えられない」
contexts.english: "That's a good way of putting it. Normally, that wouldn't be possible, but Saber's magical energy must be powerful enough to change the flow of a river. Otherwise there's no chance she'd be able to go up against Berserker with that tiny frame of hers."

counterexamples.description: The gasoline-engine model stays distinct from a recorded pseudo-immortality exception.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Ordinary Master support is fuel consumption; a past Master physically fused with a Servant and lived while it lived.
counterexamples.explanation: The gasoline-engine model stays distinct from a recorded pseudo-immortality exception.

contexts.japanese: 「マスターとサーヴァントの繋がりなんて、ガソリンとエンジンみたいなものだもの。こっちが魔力を提供して、あっちがそれを食べるだけ。
contexts.english: "The connection between Master and Servant is like gas and an engine. We provide the energy for them to consume.

contexts.japanese: ……まあ中には肉体面でもサーヴァントと共融して擬似的な“不死”を得たマスターもいたそうよ。サーヴァントが死なない限り自分も死なない、なんていうヤツなんだけど……衛宮くん、人の話聞いてる？」
contexts.english: ...Though, I've read that a Master once acquired pseudo-immortality by physically fusing with their Servant. They wouldn't die as long as their Servant doesn't die... Are you listening, Emiya?"

counterexamples.description: Rin's warning about unknown extra healing costs remains speculative.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She is certain something besides Saber's mana is consumed but jokes through possible lifespan, luck and savings.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin's warning about unknown extra healing costs remains speculative.

contexts.japanese: 「バカね、そんな理由じゃないわよ。断言してもいいけど、貴方の傷を治すと減るのはセイバーの魔力だけじゃない。
contexts.english: "That's not the point, dummy. Let me be clear: it costs more than Saber's magical energy to heal your wounds.

contexts.japanese: —貴方、それ絶対なんか使ってるわ。
contexts.english: You're giving something up when it happens.

contexts.japanese: 寿命とか勝負運とか預金残高とか、ともかく何かが減りまくってるに違いないんだから」
contexts.english: Whether that's your life, your luck, or even your bank account, you can bet that kind of healing doesn't come cheap."

counterexamples.description: Servants' Grail motive remains a condition of answering summons.
counterexamples.sourceReading: They seek the Grail and accept human summoning for that opportunity.
counterexamples.explanation: Servants' Grail motive remains a condition of answering summons.

contexts.japanese: 「サーヴァントの目的も聖杯だから。
contexts.english: "Because the Servants also seek the Holy Grail.

contexts.japanese: 彼等は聖杯を手に入れる、という条件だからこそ人間の召喚に応じているのよ」
contexts.english: One of the conditions for them allowing a Master to summon them is getting a chance at the Holy Grail."

counterexamples.description: Rin reverses Shirou's naive causal model of summoning.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Servants do not exist merely to help Masters obtain the Grail; the Grail chance motivates their answer.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin reverses Shirou's naive causal model of summoning.

contexts.japanese: 「聖杯を手に入れる為にマスターがサーヴァントを呼びだす、じゃない。
contexts.english: "Masters don't summon Servants to help them get the Holy Grail.

contexts.japanese: 聖杯が手に入るからサーヴァントはマスターの呼びだしに応じるのよ」
contexts.english: Servants answer the Masters' call to have a chance at the Holy Grail."

counterexamples.description: Servants can independently target Masters and cannot steal Command Spells.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Because they cannot neutralize rivals by taking seals, killing is their only direct method.
counterexamples.explanation: Servants can independently target Masters and cannot steal Command Spells.

contexts.japanese: 「だからサーヴァントはマスターが命令しなくとも他のマスターを消しにかかる。聖杯を手に入れるのは一人だけ。自分のマスター以外に聖杯が渡るのは彼らだって承知できないのよ。
contexts.english: "That's why Servants will go out and eliminate other Masters even without being ordered to. Only one person can get the Holy Grail. They won't allow it to fall into the hands of anyone other than their own Master.

contexts.japanese: マスターと違って、サーヴァントには令呪を奪う、なんてコトはできない。彼らが他のマスターを無力化するには殺す以外に方法がない」
contexts.english: Unlike Masters, Servants don't have the power to take away Command Spells. The only way they can neutralize other Masters is by killing them."

counterexamples.description: Return after Servant death does not erase Shirou's objection to a human-shaped death.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Rin explains return to the original place; Shirou still objects to the enacted death in this world.
counterexamples.explanation: Return after Servant death does not erase Shirou's objection to a human-shaped death.

contexts.japanese: 「あ、その点は安心して。サーヴァントに生死はないから。サーヴァントは絶命しても本来の場所に帰るだけだもの。英霊っていうのはもう死んでも死なない現象だからね。戦いに敗れて殺されるのは、当事者であるマスターだけよ」
contexts.english: "Oh, don't worry about that. Servants aren't mortal, so if they die, they'll just go back to where they came from. Heroic Spirits are phenomena that can't die. Only Masters can actually get killed when they lose a fight."

contexts.japanese: たとえ仮初めの死だとしても。
contexts.english: Even if their deaths are figurative...

contexts.japanese: この世界で、人の姿をしたモノが息絶えるという事に変わりはない。
contexts.english: It doesn't change the fact that something which takes the form of a human dies in this world.

counterexamples.description: Ordinary invisibility, physical-world interference and modern-weapon limits remain connected.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Servants unseen by those without sensitivity can still act physically, while modern weapons cannot affect spirit bodies.
counterexamples.explanation: Ordinary invisibility, physical-world interference and modern-weapon limits remain connected.

contexts.japanese: 霊感のない人間には姿さえ観測できない。
contexts.english: Humans who lack the ability to sense the supernatural can't even see them.

contexts.japanese: にも関わらず実体を持つかのように現世に干渉できるという時点で、サーヴァントは最強の兵器と言えるだろう。
contexts.english: But as soon as Servants materialize, they can interact with the physical world. You could say they're the ultimate weapons.

contexts.japanese: なにしろ今の科学では、霊体に効果のある兵器など存在しない。
contexts.english: No modern technology or weaponry can affect a spiritual form.

counterexamples.description: Completed Servant forms remain unable to grow while mana remains a separate fuel variable.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Rin distinguishes fixed development from resource supply and compares it to mages.
counterexamples.explanation: Completed Servant forms remain unable to grow while mana remains a separate fuel variable.

contexts.japanese: 「一つ言い忘れていたけど、サーヴァントっていうのは霊なの。彼等はもう完成したものだから、今以上の成長はない。
contexts.english: "I should have mentioned this sooner, but Servants are spirits. Their forms are complete, static, so they do not grow.

contexts.japanese: けど燃料である魔力は別よ。
contexts.english: But they still need magical energy as fuel.

contexts.japanese: そのあたりはわたしたち魔術師と一緒なんだけど……貴方、この意味解る？」
contexts.english: That's not unlike us mages, actually... Do you see what I'm getting at?"

counterexamples.description: Masters remain the supplement to a Servant's internal mana.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Servants do not draw ambient mana like mages and can express only power supported by their own and their Master's supply.
counterexamples.explanation: Masters remain the supplement to a Servant's internal mana.

contexts.japanese: 「そうよ。けどサーヴァント達は私たちみたいに自然から魔力を提供されてる訳じゃない。基本的に、彼らは自分の中だけの魔力で活動する。
contexts.english: "That's right. But Servants can't draw mana from the atmosphere like us. They generally run only on the magical energy within them.

contexts.japanese: それを補充するのがわたしたちマスターで、サーヴァントは自分の魔力プラス、主であるマスターの魔力分しか生前の力を発揮できないの」
contexts.english: It's our job as Masters to supplement that energy. Their power is limited by their own energy supply, plus whatever their Masters give them."

counterexamples.description: Natural and human spirits keep different implied food sources.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Rin leads Shirou from nature spirits drawing on nature to Servants drawing on human beings.
counterexamples.explanation: Natural and human spirits keep different implied food sources.

contexts.japanese: 「簡単でしょ。自然霊は自然そのものから力を汲み取る。
contexts.english: "Simple. Spirits of nature can take in power from nature itself.

contexts.japanese: なら人間霊であるサーヴァントは、一体何から力を汲み取ると思う？」
contexts.english: So what do you think Servants, who are human spirits, get power from?"

contexts.japanese: 俺たちが肉を食べるように、人の霊である彼らはつまり—
contexts.english: Just as we eat meat, human spirits like Servants have to eat...

counterexamples.description: Souls and primal emotions remain convertible fuel rather than a vague life force.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Rin names both sources and says some Masters sacrifice people for efficiency.
counterexamples.explanation: Souls and primal emotions remain convertible fuel rather than a vague life force.

contexts.japanese: 「サーヴァントは人間の原感情や魂を魔力に変換する。
contexts.english: "Servants can convert souls and primal human emotions into magical energy.

contexts.japanese: 自分のサーヴァントを強くしたいのならそれが一番効率がいい。人間を殺してサーヴァントへの生贄にするマスターは、けっして少なくないわ」
contexts.english: If you want your Servant to get stronger, that's the most efficient way. It's not rare for Masters to sacrifice humans to their Servant."

counterexamples.description: Shirou's mass-killing question and Rin's qualified response remain hypothetical.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He asks about unscrupulous Masters; Rin says maybe, then argues an intelligent one would avoid waste.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's mass-killing question and Rin's qualified response remain hypothetical.

contexts.japanese: 「生贄にするって……それじゃ手段を選ばないヤツがマスターなら、サーヴァントを強くする為に人を殺しまくるってコトなのか」
contexts.english: "Sacrifice... Are you saying there might be Masters out there who go around killing people to make their Servants stronger, if they're not choosy about their methods?"

contexts.japanese: 「そうね。けど頭のいいヤツならそんな無駄な事はしないんじゃないかな」
contexts.english: "Maybe. But I can't see a smart Master doing something like that."

counterexamples.description: Capacity, Association intervention and identity leakage all limit predation.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Rin gives separate resource, institutional and tactical reasons against conspicuous murder.
counterexamples.explanation: Capacity, Association intervention and identity leakage all limit predation.

contexts.japanese: 「いい、サーヴァントがいくら強力でも、魔力の器そのものには限界がある。能力値以上の貯蔵はできないんだから、殺して回るにしても限度があるわ。
contexts.english: "No matter how strong a Servant is, they're still limited by energy capacity. They can't store any energy above a hard limit, so there's only so much they can benefit from mass murder.

contexts.japanese: それにあからさまに殺人を犯せば協会が黙ってないし、なによりその死因からサーヴァントの能力と正体が、他のマスターたちにバレかねない。もちろんマスター自身の正体もね。
contexts.english: For one thing, the Association won't just turn a blind eye to someone going around murdering people, but more importantly, the other Masters will be able to figure out the Servant's abilities and identity based on the victims' cause of death. That, and they'll work out the other Master's identity too.

counterexamples.description: Shirou sees Rin as the person who best understands Illya because both are born mages and Rin monitors her health.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The kinship and practical care remain distinct.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou sees Rin as the person who best understands Illya because both are born mages and Rin monitors her health.

contexts.japanese: イリヤを一番良く分かってやれるのは俺でも桜でもなく遠坂なのだ。
contexts.english: Tohsaka understands Illya much better than Sakura or I do.

contexts.japanese: イリヤの体を定期的に看てくれている、という事もあるが、なによりイリヤと遠坂は生粋の魔術師である。
contexts.english: It's not just that she periodically checks in on Illya's health. Tohsaka and Illya are both proper mages.

counterexamples.description: Kiritsugu seriously tells the child he is a magician before bringing him home.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The popular word remains in his direct speech without added technical certification.
counterexamples.explanation: Kiritsugu seriously tells the child he is a magician before bringing him home.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-00:page23:1
contexts.japanese: 「おっと、大切なコトを言い忘れた。
contexts.english: "Ah. I forgot to mention one important thing.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-00:page23:1
contexts.japanese: うちに来る前に、一つだけ教えなくちゃいけないコトがある」
contexts.english: Before you come with me, there's one thing you need to know."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-00:page23:1
contexts.japanese: 初めに言っておくとね、僕は魔法使いなんだ」
contexts.english: Let me be direct with you. I'm a magician."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-00:page23:1
contexts.japanese: ホントに本気で、仰々しくそいつは言った。
contexts.english: He said it in a serious, almost ceremonious manner.

counterexamples.description: A second dream marker moves roughly eight years back to Shirou talking Kiritsugu into apprenticeship.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou, not Kiritsugu, initiates the training relationship.
counterexamples.explanation: A second dream marker moves roughly eight years back to Shirou talking Kiritsugu into apprenticeship.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-00:page27:1
contexts.japanese: ………夢を見ている。
contexts.english: ...I'm dreaming.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-00:page28:1
contexts.japanese: 幼い頃の話。
contexts.english: It's from my childhood.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-00:page28:1
contexts.japanese: ちょうど親父を言い負かして弟子にしてもらった頃だから、今から八年ぐらい前だろう。
contexts.english: It's probably about eight years ago, since it's about the time when I talked my old man into making me his apprentice.

counterexamples.description: Shirou calls his five years of training progressless and below the starting line, then rejects rushing and returns to attainable work.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The harsh ability judgment remains his self-assessment.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou calls his five years of training progressless and below the starting line, then rejects rushing and returns to attainable work.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-00:page70:1
contexts.japanese: 切嗣のようになるのだと日々修練してきたけど、現実はうまくいかない。
contexts.english: I trained every day to become like Kiritsugu, but that's easier said than done.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-00:page70:1
contexts.japanese: 初めから素質がなかったから当然と言えば当然なのだが、それでも五年間まったく進歩がない、というのは考え物だろう。
contexts.english: It's not surprising, since I didn't have what it takes from the start. But the fact that I haven't improved at all these past five years forces me to reassess things.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-00:page70:1
contexts.japanese: 現状を一言で表すなら、理想が高すぎてスタート地点にさえ立てていない、といったところ。
contexts.english: If I had to sum up my current situation, I'd say I set the bar too high. I haven't even reached the starting line.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-00:page71:1
contexts.japanese: いや、焦ってもいい事はないか。
contexts.english: No, rushing won't do me any good.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-00:page71:1
contexts.japanese: とりあえず、今は出来る事を確実にこなしていくだけだ。
contexts.english: For now, I just have to do what I can.

counterexamples.description: Shirou notices Issei's odd formal Japanese and asks him to leave; Issei exits quietly to avoid interference.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The misunderstanding remains qualified.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou notices Issei's odd formal Japanese and asks him to leave; Issei exits quietly to avoid interference.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page11:1
contexts.japanese: 「おかしな日本語使うね、一成。
contexts.english: "You say some weird stuff, Issei.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page11:1
contexts.japanese: ……っと、もう少しで済むから、ちょっと外に出ててくれ」
contexts.english: Oh hey. I'm almost done, so go ahead and step out."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page11:1
contexts.japanese: 「うむ、衛宮の邪魔はせん」
contexts.english: "Got it. I won't get in your way."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page12:1
contexts.japanese: 静かに教室から出ていく一成。
contexts.english: Issei quietly steps out of the classroom.

counterexamples.description: Touch-based internal sight is distinguished from ordinary visual diagnosis.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou closes normal vision and receives one internal image.
counterexamples.explanation: Touch-based internal sight is distinguished from ordinary visual diagnosis.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page13:1
contexts.japanese: 「……いや、デリケートと言えばデリケートなんだけど……」
contexts.english: "Well, I guess you can call it sensitive work..."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page13:1
contexts.japanese: 古びた電気ストーブに手を触れる。
contexts.english: I put my hand to the old electric stove.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page13:1
contexts.japanese: 普通、この手の修理に慣れているからと言って、見るだけでは故障箇所は判断できない。
contexts.english: No matter how long someone's been fixing things, they can't usually figure out what's wrong by sight.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page13:1
contexts.japanese: それが判るという事は、俺のやっている事は普通じゃないってことだ。
contexts.english: So the fact that I can means what I'm doing is not ordinary.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page14:1
contexts.japanese: 視覚を閉じて、触覚でストーブの中身を視る。
contexts.english: I close my eyes and "look" inside the stove by touch.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page14:1
contexts.japanese: 頭の中に湧き上がってくる一つのイメージ。
contexts.english: A single image pops into my head.

counterexamples.description: Two nearly broken heating wires, a usable heating element and a tape-manageable cord remain separately diagnosed.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The damage fits the tools on hand.
counterexamples.explanation: Two nearly broken heating wires, a usable heating element and a tape-manageable cord remain separately diagnosed.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page15:1
contexts.japanese: 「……電熱線が断線しかかってるのが二つと……電熱管はまだ保つな……電源コードの方は絶縁テープでなんとかなる……」
contexts.english: "...There are two places where the wire's about to break... The electrical pipes should last a bit longer... The power cord should be fine with just insulation tape..."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page15:1
contexts.japanese: ……良かった、手持ちの工具だけで修理できる破損内容だ。
contexts.english: Good. I should be able to fix it with just the tools I brought along.

counterexamples.description: Strengthening remains a conditional fallback not used here; Shirou then opens the cover and performs ordinary repair.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The physical work follows magical diagnosis.
counterexamples.explanation: Strengthening remains a conditional fallback not used here; Shirou then opens the cover and performs ordinary repair.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page16:1
contexts.japanese: 電熱管がイカレていたら素人の手には負えない。
contexts.english: If the electrical pipes were broken, it wouldn't be fixable by an amateur.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page16:1
contexts.japanese: その時は素人じゃない方法で“強化”しなくてはいけなかったが、これなら内部を視るだけで十分だ。
contexts.english: Had that been the case, a certain "Strengthening" would have to be done, which no amateur could manage, but I should be able to fix this one by sight.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page16:1
contexts.japanese: それが切嗣に教わった、衛宮士郎の“魔術”である。
contexts.english: This is the magecraft Kiritsugu taught me.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page17:1
contexts.japanese: カバーを外して内部線の修理に取りかかる。
contexts.english: I take off the cover to begin my repairs.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page17:1
contexts.japanese: 破損箇所はもう判っているんだから、あとの作業は簡単だ。
contexts.english: I already know where it's broken, so the rest of the work is easy.

counterexamples.description: Shirou's no-talent self-assessment coexists with exceptional blueprint visualization and Kiritsugu's surprise.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Useless remains Kiritsugu's quoted evaluation.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's no-talent self-assessment coexists with exceptional blueprint visualization and Kiritsugu's surprise.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page18:1
contexts.japanese: そう。衛宮士郎に魔術の才能はまったく無かった。
contexts.english: That's right. I, Shirou Emiya, have absolutely no talent in magecraft.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page18:1
contexts.japanese: その代わりといってはなんだが、物の構造、さっきみたいに設計図を連想する事だけはバカみたいに巧いと思う。
contexts.english: But, for some reason, I have a knack for visualizing the structure of things or blueprints, like I did just now.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page18:1
contexts.japanese: 実際、設計図を連想して再現した時なんて、親父は目を丸くして驚いた後、「なんて無駄な才能だ」なんて嘆いていたっけ。
contexts.english: My old man once saw me imagine and recreate a blueprint. He looked surprised, then muttered, "What a useless talent."

counterexamples.description: Ordinary mages target the central core rather than surveying the full structure.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The blueprint method is explicitly more laborious.
counterexamples.explanation: Ordinary mages target the central core rather than surveying the full structure.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page19:1
contexts.japanese: 本来の魔術師なら、先ほどのようにわざわざ隅々まで構造を把握する、なんていう必要はない。
contexts.english: A mage normally wouldn't need to survey an object's entire structure like I do.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page20:1
contexts.japanese: 物事の核である中心を即座に読みとり、誰よりも速く変化させるのが魔術師たちの戦いだと言う。
contexts.english: He claims the mage's struggle is to instantly seek out an object's center, or its core, and transform it as quickly as possible.

counterexamples.description: Rapid fault location still requires practical repair skill and is limited to amateur-fixable junk.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The scene does not grant unlimited repair power.
counterexamples.explanation: Rapid fault location still requires practical repair skill and is limited to amateur-fixable junk.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page21:1
contexts.japanese: そんなこんなで、自分の得意な分野はこういった故障品の修理だったりする訳だ。
contexts.english: And so, fixing broken stuff is one of the only things I'm good at.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page21:1
contexts.japanese: なにしろ解体して患部を探し出す必要がない。
contexts.english: After all, I don't have to open the entire thing up to find the problem.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page21:1
contexts.japanese: すみやかに故障箇所を探し出せるなら、あとは直す技術を持っていれば大抵の物は直せるだろう。
contexts.english: If I can find the problem quickly, I can fix most things as long as I have the know-how to repair it.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page21:1
contexts.japanese: ま、それもこういった『ちょっとした素人知識』で直せてしまうガラクタに限るのだが。
contexts.english: Though, I only do that with things an amateur could reasonably be expected to fix.

counterexamples.description: Shirou alone narrates knowledge of Kiritsugu's mage identity, hides his apprenticeship and calls himself half-trained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: His self-assessment is not expanded into universal character knowledge.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou alone narrates knowledge of Kiritsugu's mage identity, hides his apprenticeship and calls himself half-trained.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page25:1
contexts.japanese: ……とは言っても、親父が魔術師だったのを知っているのは俺だけだ。
contexts.english: But at the same time, I'm the only one who knows that my old man was a mage.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page25:1
contexts.japanese: 曰く、魔術師はその正体を隠すもの。
contexts.english: They say mages have to keep that part of their lives secret.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page25:1
contexts.japanese: だから親父に弟子入りした俺も、魔術を学んでいる事は隠している。
contexts.english: Which is why I've also been hiding from others that I'm learning magecraft after I became my old man's apprentice.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page26:1
contexts.japanese: ただ、学んでいると言っても満足な魔術は何一つも使えない半人前だ。
contexts.english: "Learning" may be a bit of a stretch, really, since I can barely use magecraft properly.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page26:1
contexts.japanese: そんな俺が魔術を隠そうが隠すまいが大差はないだろうが、一応遺言でもあるし、こうして隠しながら日々鍛練を続けてきた訳である。
contexts.english: So it wouldn't make much of a difference whether I hide magecraft or not, but since it was my old man's dying wish, I've been training in secret.

counterexamples.description: The nearby Western homes lead into childhood rumors of a scary magician, which Sakura once took seriously.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The rumor is not converted into current proof of the setting's formal magic system.
counterexamples.explanation: The nearby Western homes lead into childhood rumors of a scary magician, which Sakura once took seriously.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page23:1
contexts.japanese: 「そういう桜は？　同じ洋館だし、もしかして近所づきあいとかあるのか？」
contexts.english: "What about you? You two both live in Western houses in the same neighborhood, so do you ever talk?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page23:1
contexts.japanese: 「ないですよ。たしかに近所ではありますけど、遠坂先輩のお家は坂の上ですから。
contexts.english: "We do not. We may live close to each other, but Miss Tohsaka's home is higher up on the hill.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page23:1
contexts.japanese: けど、遠坂先輩のお家が洋館だって知ってるんですね、先輩」
contexts.english: But how did you know Miss Tohsaka's home is a Western house?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page24:1
contexts.japanese: 「ああ、ちょっと小耳に挟んだんだ。遠坂んところは幽霊屋敷だとかなんとか。幽霊屋敷っていったら洋館と相場が決まってるだろ」
contexts.english: "I heard a rumor about Tohsaka's house being a haunted mansion or something. And you would think a haunted mansion would be more of a Western house."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page25:1
contexts.japanese: 「そうですね。遠坂先輩は一人が好きみたいですから。わたしも子供の頃、坂の上には怖い魔法使いが住んでるって言われてました」
contexts.english: "You're right. I believe Miss Tohsaka likes to keep to herself, and when I was little, I was told that there was a scary magician living on top of the hill."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page26:1
contexts.japanese: 「へえ、怖い魔法使いか。俺もそんなふうな噂は聞いたな。まあ、それ言ったら洋館側の家はみんな魔法使いが住んでいそうだけど。で、桜は信じたのか、その話？」
contexts.english: "A scary magician, huh? I think I heard that rumor too. Though, all the Western houses on that side of town seem like there would be magicians living in them. So did you believe those rumors, Sakura?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page27:1
contexts.japanese: 「信じました。だって子供だったんです。だから、坂の上には行っちゃいけないって、いつも思ってました」
contexts.english: "I did. I was a child, after all. That's why I always avoided going all the way up the hill."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page27:1
contexts.japanese: 面白半分で聞いたコトに、桜は真剣な顔で答えていた。
contexts.english: I was only asking half-jokingly, but her response seems to have been in earnest.

counterexamples.description: Just before midnight Shirou begins his habitual inward-focused practice rather than going to sleep.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Breathing and attention precede circuit induction.
counterexamples.explanation: Just before midnight Shirou begins his habitual inward-focused practice rather than going to sleep.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page0:1
contexts.japanese: そうして一日が終わる。
contexts.english: And that is how my day ends.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page0:1
contexts.japanese: 深夜零時前、衛宮士郎は日課になっている“魔術”を行わなくてはならない。
contexts.english: Just before midnight, Shirou Emiya must perform the daily routine of utilizing magecraft.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page1:1
contexts.japanese: 結跏趺坐に姿勢をとり、呼吸を整える。
contexts.english: I cross my legs, take my position, and regulate my breathing.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page1:1
contexts.japanese: 頭の中はできるだけ白紙に。
contexts.english: I try to empty my mind.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page1:1
contexts.japanese: 外界との接触はさけ、意識は全て内界に向ける。
contexts.english: I ignore everything around me and turn my focus inward.

counterexamples.description: Trace On remains an incantation functioning as self-directed conditioning for a practitioner without crest or broad magical education.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The passage does not declare all incantations meaningless.
counterexamples.explanation: Trace On remains an incantation functioning as self-directed conditioning for a practitioner without crest or broad magical education.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page2:1
contexts.japanese: 「—同調、開始」
contexts.english: "Trace On."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page2:1
contexts.japanese: 否、それは本当に自己暗示にすぎない。
contexts.english: No, this is a kind of hypnosis.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page2:1
contexts.japanese: 魔術刻印とやらがなく、魔道の知識もない自分にとって、呪文は自分を変革させる為だけの物だ。
contexts.english: With no Magic Crest and no magical knowledge, the incantation I mutter is really just a way to focus myself and change my body.

counterexamples.description: Ordinary humans lack the relevant mana-carrying nerve, so Shirou creates one temporarily through a genuinely painful bodily process.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The rod's pain is not dismissed as metaphor.
counterexamples.explanation: Ordinary humans lack the relevant mana-carrying nerve, so Shirou creates one temporarily through a genuinely painful bodily process.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page3:1
contexts.japanese: ……本来、人間の体に魔力を通す神経はない。
contexts.english: Typically, humans do not have any lines which allow magical energy to pass through their body.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page4:1
contexts.japanese: 魔術は自己との戦いだ。
contexts.english: Magecraft is a battle with yourself.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page4:1
contexts.japanese: 例えば、この瞬間、背骨に焼けた鉄の棒を突き刺していく。
contexts.english: For example, I insert a burning steel rod into my backbone.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page4:1
contexts.japanese: その鉄の棒こそ、たった一本だけ用意できる自分の“魔術回路”だ。
contexts.english: The steel rod itself is the one and only Magic Circuit I can prepare for myself.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page5:1
contexts.japanese: それは比喩ではない。
contexts.english: This is not a metaphor.

counterexamples.description: Young Shirou admires Kiritsugu, begs for instruction, lacks natural talent and remains ignorant of why Kiritsugu withheld magical knowledge.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Later explanations are not projected into the child's understanding.
counterexamples.explanation: Young Shirou admires Kiritsugu, begs for instruction, lacks natural talent and remains ignorant of why Kiritsugu withheld magical knowledge.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page6:1
contexts.japanese: —僕は魔法使いなんだ。
contexts.english: I'm a magician.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page6:1
contexts.japanese: そう言った衛宮切嗣は、本当に魔術師だった。
contexts.english: Kiritsugu Emiya was a mage.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page6:1
contexts.japanese: 数々の神秘を学び、世界の構造とやらに肉薄し、奇跡を実行する生粋の魔術師。
contexts.english: He was a true mage who disciplined himself in a wide variety of Mystics, plumbed the deeper secrets of the world and its workings, and even performed miracles.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page6:1
contexts.japanese: その切嗣に憧れて、とにかく魔術を教えてくれとねだった幼い自分。
contexts.english: And as a young child I admired Kiritsugu, and begged him to teach me magecraft.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page7:1
contexts.japanese: で、もちろん俺には持って生まれた才能なんてないし、切嗣は魔道の知識なんて教えてはくれなかった。
contexts.english: I obviously never had that inborn talent, and Kiritsugu never imparted any knowledge about magecraft to me.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page7:1
contexts.japanese: なんでも、そんなモノは君には必要ない、とかなんとか。
contexts.english: I was told it wasn't necessary for me... Something like that.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page8:1
contexts.japanese: 今でもその言葉の意味は判らない。
contexts.english: I still don't understand what he meant by that.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page8:1
contexts.japanese: それでも、子供だった自分にはどうでも良かったのだろう。
contexts.english: But it didn't matter to me as a child.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page8:1
contexts.japanese: ともかく魔術さえ使えれば、切嗣のようになれると思ったのだ。
contexts.english: I always thought learning magecraft would bring me that much closer to being like Kiritsugu.

counterexamples.description: Magic Circuits and the bloodline-transmitted Magic Crest remain distinct; adoption prevents crest transfer, and Shirou admits he does not know what a crest is.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The scene does not say adoption prevents all magecraft.
counterexamples.explanation: Magic Circuits and the bloodline-transmitted Magic Crest remain distinct; adoption prevents crest transfer, and Shirou admits he does not know what a crest is.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page9:1
contexts.japanese: しかし、持って生まれた才能—魔術回路とやらの多さも、代々積み重ねてきた魔術の業も俺にはなかった。
contexts.english: I was blessed neither with talent—that is, an abundance of Magic Circuits within me—nor was generations of magecraft knowledge handed down to me.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page10:1
contexts.japanese: 切嗣の持っていた魔術の業……衛宮の家に伝わっていた魔術刻印とやらは、肉親にしか移植できないモノなのだそうだ。
contexts.english: The magecraft Kiritsugu possessed...the Magic Crest passed down from the Emiya family, can only be passed on to a blood relative.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page10:1
contexts.japanese: だから養子である俺には、衛宮家の刻印は受け取れなかった。
contexts.english: As an adopted son, I could not receive the Emiya family's crest.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page11:1
contexts.japanese: いやまあ。
contexts.english: Then again...

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page11:1
contexts.japanese: 実際、魔術刻印っていう物がなんなのか知らない俺から見れば、そんなのが有ろうが無かろうがこれっぽっちも関係ない話ではある。
contexts.english: ...since I honestly don't have any idea what the hell a Magic Crest even is, it doesn't matter much whether I have one or not.

counterexamples.description: The exposition distinguishes life-force-like magical energy, mana, od, external drawing, conversion and Magic Circuits.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The claims remain Shirou's received account rather than independently authenticated universal law.
counterexamples.explanation: The exposition distinguishes life-force-like magical energy, mana, od, external drawing, conversion and Magic Circuits.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page12:1
contexts.japanese: 魔術師になりたいのなら、俺自身が持っている特質に応じた魔術を習うしかない。
contexts.english: If I want to be a mage, I just have to learn magecraft that suits the traits that I do have.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page13:1
contexts.japanese: 魔術とは、極端に言って魔力を放出する技術なのだという。
contexts.english: Magecraft is, taken to its extreme, a skill supposedly meant to release magical energy.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page13:1
contexts.japanese: 魔力とは生命力と言い換えてもいい。
contexts.english: You could say that magical energy is a life force.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page13:1
contexts.japanese: 魔力は世界に満ちている大源と、生物の中で生成される小源に分かれる。
contexts.english: Magical energy is separated into two sources: mana, which comes from the world's atmosphere, and od, which is created within living creatures.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page14:1
contexts.japanese: 大源、小源というからには、小より大のが優れているのは言うまでもない。
contexts.english: Obviously mana, which comes from the world itself, is superior to od.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page14:1
contexts.japanese: 人間一人が作る魔力である小源と、世界に満ちている魔力である大源では力の度合いが段違いだ。
contexts.english: The sheer power of the world's mana is simply not even comparable to the od one human can create.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page14:1
contexts.japanese: どのような魔術であれ、大源をもちいる魔術は個人で行う魔術をたやすく凌駕する。
contexts.english: No matter the form it takes, magecraft utilizing mana will always surpass anything created from an individual's od.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page15:1
contexts.japanese: そういったワケで、優れた魔術師は世界から魔力を汲み上げる術に長けている。
contexts.english: So a powerful mage is one who excels at drawing magical energy from the world.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page15:1
contexts.japanese: それは濾過器のイメージに近い。
contexts.english: It's a lot like a filtration system.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page15:1
contexts.japanese: 魔術師は自身の体を変換回路にして、外界から魔力を汲み上げて人間でも使えるモノ、にするのだ。
contexts.english: A mage will use their own body's circuits to draw in mana from outside and convert it into something usable.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page15:1
contexts.japanese: この変換回路を、魔術師は魔術回路と呼ぶ。
contexts.english: Mages call the circuits they use to accomplish this "Magic Circuits."

counterexamples.description: Circuit count is fixed at birth and mage lineages shape descendants, while Shirou infers low prospects from an ordinary family.
counterexamples.sourceReading: His actual circuit count is not supplied here.
counterexamples.explanation: Circuit count is fixed at birth and mage lineages shape descendants, while Shirou infers low prospects from an ordinary family.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page16:1
contexts.japanese: これこそが生まれつきの才能というヤツで、魔術回路の数は生まれた瞬間に決まっている。
contexts.english: This is the inborn talent part. The number of Magic Circuits one has is determined at the moment of birth.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page16:1
contexts.japanese: だから魔術師は何代も血を重ね、生まれてくる子孫たちを、より魔術に適した肉体にする。
contexts.english: That's why mages will spend generations trying to ensure their descendants have a body more suitable for magic.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page16:1
contexts.japanese: いきすぎた家系は品種改良じみた真似までして、生まれてくる子供の魔術回路を増やすのだとか。
contexts.english: Some families even go as far as to practice selective breeding in order to increase the number of Magic Circuits in their children.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page17:1
contexts.japanese: ……まあ、そんな訳で普通の家庭に育った俺には、多くの魔術回路を望むべくもなかった。
contexts.english: And since I was raised in a normal family, I never had a chance of having much in the way of Magic Circuits.

counterexamples.description: Kiritsugu's origin-based aptitude teaching remains partly incomprehensible to Shirou, and the apprenticeship began eight years earlier.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kiritsugu is not presented as enthusiastically recruiting a successor.
counterexamples.explanation: Kiritsugu's origin-based aptitude teaching remains partly incomprehensible to Shirou, and the apprenticeship began eight years earlier.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page18:1
contexts.japanese: そうなると残された手段は一つ。
contexts.english: That left me only one option.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page18:1
contexts.japanese: 切嗣曰く、どんな人間にも一つぐらいは適性のある魔術系統があるらしい。
contexts.english: According to Kiritsugu, everyone is well-suited to one specific form of magecraft.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page18:1
contexts.japanese: その人間の“起源”に従って魔力を引き出す、と言っていたけど、そのあたりの話はちんぷんかんぷんだ。
contexts.english: He also said something about drawing out magical energy based on the person's "origin," but I never quite understood that part.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page19:1
contexts.japanese: だから、ただその魔術だけを教わった。
contexts.english: And that's why I've only learned this one magecraft.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page19:1
contexts.japanese: それが八年前の話。
contexts.english: That was eight years ago.

counterexamples.description: Kiritsugu warns that magecraft leaves ordinary morality, approaches killing and death, and is a path of self-destruction; child Shirou nods without fear.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The warning remains Kiritsugu's speech.
counterexamples.explanation: Kiritsugu warns that magecraft leaves ordinary morality, approaches killing and death, and is a path of self-destruction; child Shirou nods without fear.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page20:1
contexts.japanese: —いいかい士郎。魔術を習う、という事は常識からかけ離れるという事だ。死ぬ時は死に、殺す時は殺す。
contexts.english: Listen, Shirou. Learning magecraft means leaving behind common sense. You die when the end comes for you, and you kill when you must.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page20:1
contexts.japanese: 僕たちの本質は生ではなく死だからね。魔術とは、自らを滅ぼす道に他ならない—
contexts.english: Life isn't at the core of what we do, death is. Magecraft is walking the path of self-destruction.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page21:1
contexts.japanese: 幼い心は恐れを知らなかったのだろう。
contexts.english: I guess I knew no fear as a child.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page21:1
contexts.japanese: 強く頷く衛宮士郎の頭に、切嗣は仕方なげに手を置いて苦笑していた。
contexts.english: Kiritsugu smiled bitterly, placing a hand atop my head as I nodded enthusiastically.

counterexamples.description: Secrecy and training are subordinate to using magecraft only for others; the resulting magic user is distinguished from a mage, and Shirou says he admired Kiritsugu rather than mages.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The hierarchy and later inference remain visible.
counterexamples.explanation: Secrecy and training are subordinate to using magecraft only for others; the resulting magic user is distinguished from a mage, and Shirou says he admired Kiritsugu rather than mages.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page22:1
contexts.japanese: —君に教えるのは、そういった争いを呼ぶ類の物だ。
contexts.english: What I'm about to teach you is the sort of thing that could cause conflict.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page22:1
contexts.japanese: だから人前で使ってはいけないし、難しい物だから鍛錬を怠ってもいけない。
contexts.english: So you should never use it in front of anyone, and you should never forget your training, because it's difficult.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page22:1
contexts.japanese: でもまあ、それは破ったって構わない。
contexts.english: Then again, you don't really need to follow it either.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page22:1
contexts.japanese: 一番大事な事はね、魔術は自分の為じゃなくて他人の為だけに使う、という事だよ。そうすれば士郎は魔術使いではあるけど、魔術師ではなくなるからね—
contexts.english: The most important thing is that you always remember that magecraft is to be used for others, and not for yourself. And that would make you simply a user of magecraft, rather than a mage.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page23:1
contexts.japanese: ……切嗣は、衛宮士郎に魔術師になってほしくなかったのだろう。
contexts.english: I guess Kiritsugu didn't want me to be a mage.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page23:1
contexts.japanese: それは構わないと思う。
contexts.english: But I didn't care about that.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-15:page23:1
contexts.japanese: 俺が憧れていたのは切嗣であって魔術師じゃない。
contexts.english: I admired Kiritsugu, not mages.

counterexamples.description: A distracting thought misaligns the induced circuit; loss of breathing control would be fatal, but Shirou recovers and completes one pseudo-nerve.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Death and bodily destruction remain conditional rather than accomplished.
